text: No man shall take his father's wife, nor uncover his father's skirt.
No man whose testicles are crushed or whose organ is cut off shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
No one born of a forbidden union shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of them shall ever enter the assembly of the LORD,
because they did not come to meet you with bread and water on your journey when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam; instead, the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
You shall never seek their welfare or their good, as long as you live.
Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, for you were a stranger in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you march out to camp against your enemies, keep yourself from everything evil.

versions.text: When you march out to camp against your enemies, keep yourself from everything unclean.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew דָּבָר רָע means "evil thing" rather than specifically "unclean"; the broader wording preserves the moral as well as ritual sense, and the following verses illustrate one application.

text: If any man among you becomes unclean from an emission in the night, he shall go outside the camp; he must not come back inside it.
Toward evening he shall wash himself with water, and at sunset he may return to the camp.
You shall have a place outside the camp where you may go to relieve yourself.
And you shall keep a spade among your equipment; when you squat outside, dig a hole with it, and afterward cover up your excrement.

For the LORD your God walks about in your camp to keep you safe and to deliver your enemies to you. Therefore your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.

versions.text: For the LORD your God walks about in your camp to keep you safe and to deliver your enemies to you. Therefore your camp must be holy, so that he sees nothing indecent among you and turns away from you.
versions.explanation: As written, the clause "so that he sees nothing indecent among you and turns away from you" makes God's turning away a desired result, reversing the Hebrew. The negative must govern both verbs: he must not see anything indecent and (consequently) turn away.

text: You shall not hand a slave back to his master when he has escaped to you from that master.
He shall live with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses in one of your towns, wherever it suits him. You shall not mistreat him.
No daughter of Israel shall be a cult prostitute, and no son of Israel shall be a cult prostitute.
You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the earnings of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, for both are detestable to the LORD your God.
You shall not charge your brother interest—interest on money, interest on food, interest on anything that may be lent at interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you set your hand to in the land you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to fulfill it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and you would be guilty of sin.
But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty.
Be careful to do what your lips have promised: the freewill offering you vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you shall not put any into your basket.
When you walk into your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor's grain.
